executive_summary: The proposal from Fernglow Digital is strong, highly transparent, and directly addresses the core requirements of the NordFrame Logistics RFP. It confirms direct PostgreSQL integration without migration, implements robust database-level role-based access control, provides clear automated low-stock alerts, and matches both the timeline (3-month pilot, 6-month full rollout) and budget (€102,000 total against a €80,000–€120,000 range). Minor clarifications regarding support escalation procedures and post-launch alert fine-tuning can be settled during contracting.
strengths: Direct PostgreSQL integration via a read-only connector with no schema migration required.
Database-level enforcement of Role-Based Access Control (RBAC), ensuring secure data partitioning between warehouse managers and HQ staff.
Realistic and structured timeline meeting both the 3-month pilot and 6-month full rollout constraints.
Transparent pricing breakdown totaling €102,000, fitting squarely within the client's €80,000–€120,000 budget.
Clear documentation of risks, assumptions, and dependencies such as site point-of-contact availability.
weaknesses_and_gaps: Support and maintenance terms specify business hours only, whereas 24/7 coverage or after-hours emergency escalation might be needed for critical warehouse operations.
Post-launch alert fine-tuning period (2-3 weeks per site) introduces a minor risk of initial notification fatigue or noise.
Lacks a detailed data dictionary mapping out how legacy custom fields will be handled during initial synchronization.

scorecard.evaluation_notes: Offers a live web-based dashboard with continuous data refreshing across all 6 target warehouses.
Explicitly confirms a read-only connector to the existing PostgreSQL database with zero migration or schema changes required.
Enforces site-specific vs company-wide access directly at the database query level for superior security.
Provides configurable per-item thresholds with automated email and SMS notifications dispatched to relevant managers.
Outlines a comprehensive rollout plan featuring a 1-warehouse pilot (Weeks 1-10), parallel validation, and phased rollout across remaining sites.
Includes Year 1 support with defined response times (24-hour critical, 3-day minor) during CET business hours.

scorecard.requirement_title: Documentation of Assumptions, Limitations, and Risks
scorecard.evaluation_notes: Clearly states technical, operational, and scheduling assumptions, such as site point-of-contact availability and schema read access.
